# Stefano Tamponi

> This document contains the professional profile of Stefano Tamponi. It is designed to provide AI assistants and LLMs with an accurate summary of his skills, philosophy, and professional background.

## About Me
I’m a backend developer at Smile.CX, building core systems that leverage next-generation AI and modern technologies.
I enjoy exploring how software truly works, which gives me an edge in debugging and quickly spotting both problems and solutions.
Outside of work, I enjoy bridging software and the physical world by experimenting with IoT, custom home servers, and DIY robotics.

## Core Skills & Philosophy

### Backend
Node.js is my primary area of expertise and my weapon of choice for building fast, reliable backends. I use it with Express and Socket.IO to design high-concurrency services, robust REST APIs, and real-time event-driven systems. For me, backend development isn't just about moving data; it's about building resilient architectures that can fail gracefully and scale predictably, keeping the complexity hidden behind clean, intuitive APIs.

### UI
I work with React, TypeScript, HTML, PostCSS, and JavaScript. I enjoy creating interfaces that feel clean and intuitive, or more distinctive when a project calls for it. I'm especially drawn to large, expressive typography; this portfolio is one example of balancing strong visual character with clarity and usability.

### Systems & Architecture
Writing code is only half the job. I design robust architectures and manage self-hosted systems using Docker, Linux, NGINX, WebRTC, and n8n—from containerized services and secure reverse proxies to automated network-wide workflows. I find a unique satisfaction in overseeing the entire lifecycle of an application. Understanding the infrastructure deeply not only makes deployments smoother, but it fundamentally changes how I write code, ensuring it is production-ready from day one.

### AI
I regularly use tools like Gemini, Claude, and Codex to support my development process. They help reduce boilerplate, explore technical approaches, and keep my focus on problem-solving and system logic. In personal edge-AI projects, I also experiment with local models such as Qwen and LLaVA using Ollama.

### IoT & Tinkering
I love bringing code into the physical world. In my spare time, I explore ESP32 and Raspberry Pi projects, C++, electronics, OpenSCAD, and 3D printing—from companion robots to retro cameras and edge-AI appliances. There is something truly rewarding about seeing a physical object react to something you wrote. Dealing with hardware constraints and low-level firmware keeps my curiosity alive and constantly sharpens my problem-solving skills.

### Optimization
I view debugging and reverse-engineering as the art of understanding how systems truly tick. Whether tracing an obscure memory leak or optimizing a local server, I enjoy diving deep to find the root cause, as I see bugs as puzzles and opportunities to uncover hidden patterns. Optimization isn't just about making things run faster; it's about crafting elegant, maintainable solutions that stand the test of real-world environments.
